The Goliath is an eighty-ton quad assault BattleMech introduced in 2652 by Brigadier Corporation. Designed as a larger, more capable successor to the troubled Scorpion, the Goliath overcame the engineering challenges that had plagued earlier four-legged designs to become a quality fire-support platform. Despite its proven performance, the Goliath struggled to find buyers during the Star League era, as the stigma of earlier quad designs made it a hard sell to procurement officers accustomed to bipedal chassis. Production remained limited for over a century before the design earned renewed respect, with multiple manufacturers producing updated variants from the late 3060s onward.

The Goliath is a steady fire-support unit, with a PPC and dual LRM racks providing good ranged firepower. At 64 kph, it can keep up with heavy units and some lighter 'Mechs, while almost fifteen tons of armor let it take quite a beating. One of the strongest points of the Goliath is the number of heat sinks that allows it to keep up almost a constant rate of fire. Up close, the Goliath suffers. Dual machine guns might be good at fending off infantry, but against armored units they are almost useless, while the long-ranged weaponry is inaccurate.

The quad chassis provides superior stability when firing on the move, reducing the accuracy penalties that plague bipedal designs traversing rough terrain. This makes the Goliath an exceptional platform for sustained bombardment from elevated positions, where its wide stance keeps the weapons array level even on uneven ground. However, the quad layout limits the design's ability to mount arm-based weapons, forcing engineers to concentrate firepower in the torso and head locations. The lack of hands also means the Goliath cannot engage in melee combat or manipulate objects, a significant limitation during urban operations where versatility is prized.

Brigadier Corporation developed the Goliath in 2652 as the second of their quad BattleMech designs, building on lessons learned from the unsuccessful Scorpion and the Xanthos. While the Scorpion was not a good design, it also had to contend with the fundamental challenges of a four-legged chassis. By learning from their failures, Brigadier's engineers were not only able to overcome many of the problems that the Scorpion suffered from but also to produce a quality design. The questionable reputation of the Scorpion made the Goliath a hard sell, however, and the Star League passed on the design. After over a century of good but limited service in the Periphery and House armies, the League inquired about purchasing some Goliaths, but the deal fell through as the Amaris Coup and the dissolution of the Star League occurred.

The Goliath weighs in at 80 tons, allowing it to carry a much heavier weapons payload and armor than the Scorpion at the cost of mobility. Very few Goliaths remain from the original production run, and most of those are split between Lyran units and the Free Worlds League. The Lyran Commonwealth put a priority on maintaining their Goliaths while Corean manufactures a few new Goliaths each year. Defiance Industries makes spare parts for the Goliath and has discussed manufacturing it, but held out for an upgraded design before beginning production.

Despite the rarity of the 'Mech, it has been involved in many important battles. In a 2901 battle for Sirius, a Marik Goliath was the centerpiece in their attack on a Liao position, disabling a BattleMaster and a pair of Shadow Hawks and pushing the Capellan line back forty kilometers. During the Fourth Succession War, Captain Andrew Redburn's Delta Company annihilated the Fifth Capellan Chargers - 'Cochraine's Goliaths' - on St. Andre.

In the late 3060s the Goliath saw renewed production and renewed popularity and has since become a powerful and respected assault 'Mech. In 3143, the Corean Enterprises - MacAdams-Suharno plant on Stewart was captured by Clan Wolf, and its GOL-6M variant production line was converted to produce a Clan version of the 'Mech.

The term BattleMech conjures up images of mechanical bipedal warriors striding across the battlefield, yet quadrupedal ’Mechs have been a mainstay of civilian enterprises for centuries. The Brigadier Corporation realized the benefits of stability and maneuverability of such chassis in military roles, and it was with the culmination of their QuadMechs, the Goliath, that they sought to build their reputation. The ’Mechs height made it psychologically intimidating to conventional forces, but its specialized mechanical requirements and the vulnerability of its motive systems made it a poor fit for the Star League Army. Instead, Brigadier Corporation recouped some of the development costs via sales to the Great Houses and Periphery nations, and the ’Mech saw action throughout the Succession Wars. Following Operation Revival there was renewed interest in quads, but the Jihad and subsequent rise of the Republic limited developments to the Goliath.

House Marik intended to re-open the Goliath production facility on Oliver—defunct since the Second Succession War—but the Jihad struck. For many years the line produced IndustrialMechs, but in the wake of Gray Monday, Brigadier resumed Goliath production with the -7R model. Clan Wolf’s capture of Oliver placed the Wolf Empire in a quandary: they already build the upgraded Goliath C on Stewart, so they are unsure how best to benefit the Empire with the Oliver line. For now, it remains unmodified, while upgrade efforts are focused on the Scorpion—something we Foxes can possibly take advantage of.:br::br::tab:The directional, turret-like torso mount gives the Goliath an improved field of fire, and advanced tracking systems allow the pilot to engage multiple targets simultaneously with main and secondary weapons, a deadly advantage in many encounters. However, the complex actuator design remains a vulnerability, and the lack of credible defensive weaponry leaves some Goliaths open to close-range attacks and battle armor swarms.:br::br::tab:Osaka Heavy Metrics’ recently introduced GOL-7K has a deadly counter to such threats: M-pods concealed in the center torso and in each leg. These defenses are hidden behind blow-away panels designed to resemble maintenance hatches, providing an unwelcome surprise for anyone who gets too close. With a focus on medium-range combat, this Goliath variant is part of their expansion to add a true BattleMech to their stable of combat support quad IndustrialMechs. How and when Osaka acquired the plans is unknown, but espionage is suspected.

The Goliath’s sparse deployment meant that it saw limited action during the Succession Wars, but it often played a notable role. In 2901, a Marik Goliath led the assault against Liao positions on Sirius. It used its long-range weapons to strike at the Capellan HQ and disable three ’Mechs. This allowed the rest of the FWLM lance to push the enemy back some forty kilometers. However, for every success there was a notable failure. During the invasion of Kittery in 3005, a lance of Davion light ’Mechs surrounded and destroyed a lone Liao Goliath. It valiantly withstood the close-range assaults and eliminated two of its attackers before falling.:br::br::tab:A rediscovered Star League-era cache of Goliaths allowed the Capellan Confederation to resurrect the Fifth Capellan Chargers during the Third Succession War. Their old regimental nickname of Cochraine’s Goliaths was never more fitting. This rebuilt command came to the public’s attention during the first wave of the Fourth Succession War on St. Andre in 3028, in what became the best-known battle featuring the Goliath. The Davion Light Guards led the assault on a suspected former SLDF base, guarded by Cochraine’s Goliaths. The AFFS troops failed to gain aerospace superiority and were scattered. The battle initially went in the defenders’ favor. The much heavier Liao ’Mechs divided the invaders and began grinding them down with withering long-range fire. The Light Guards ordered a retreat, but Captain Andrew Redburn led his double-strength Delta Company—configured as a close-assault force—into the Capellans’ rear area. As on Kittery, defending the close assaults of the light ’Mechs proved challenging. Five of Cochraine’s MechWarriors fell to the lighter invaders, but the high cost threatened to collapse Redburn’s Company. A suicidal “death from above” attack killed Colonel Fiona Cochraine in her Goliath’s cockpit. Liao morale crumbled, allowing the Davion forces to annihilate the defending battalion. The post-Jihad preponderance of quads like the Goliath earned the Second St. Ives Lancers the nickname “Cochraine’s Revenge.”:br::br::tab:In the wake of Gray Monday, the Goliath was more popular than ever in both House and Republic forces. In 3146, Marik Goliaths played a key role when part of the Eighth Free Worlds Guards re-deployed from Nockatunga to Bolan in support of General Claudio Brett’s Tamarind Regulars. The intimidating assault ’Mechs provided much-needed firepower and resilience, pushing the Lyran defenders out of positions in the mountains of Sakété and securing the Brahui pass. In the assault on the Melissa Steiner Martial Academy, the Steiner forces attempted to exploit the Goliath’s actuator weakness. General Brett’s battle armor forces, operating in support of the Eighth, made short work of the LCAF troops, most of whom fled. The Eighth’s Goliaths continued to harass the withdrawing Bolan Guards. Their long-range firepower harried the retreating forces even as they boarded their DropShips, helping secure the former provincial capital for the League.:br::br::tab:The revamped Goliaths of the Republic’s Fifteenth Hastati Sentinels fought valiantly on Castor against the rampaging Wolves, but they were ultimately overwhelmed. Fighting as matched pairs, the -7Rs and -7Cs provided their own support as the Republic’s lines bent, and then buckled around them. The outmatched Goliaths fought the Golden Keshik and the Third and Fourth Wolf Battle Clusters until they fell. Their sacrifice allowed some of the Republic forces to withdraw.

Prior to the Clan Invasion, few variants of the Goliath existed, most notably the GOL-3M, first fielded in 3047. Recovered Star League technology improved the ’Mech’s performance. Post-invasion, this variant underwent minor modifications in response to the invaders, yielding most notably the GOL-3M2, which replaced the machine guns with small pulse lasers.:br::br::tab:Brigadier offered one major variant of the -7R that focused on medium-range combat, much like Osaka’s offering. A competitor to Corean’s own Phoenix Goliaths, the GOL-7C added insult to injury by mimicking Corean’s long-gone Sirocco with its Streak SRMs and Ultra AC/10. This dedicated brawler is often deployed alongside the more traditional -7R as an anti-infantry escort.:br::br::tab:Unfounded rumors indicate that the Scorpion Empire developed Goliath and Scorpion OmniMechs, following the successful pilot project based on the Snow Fox. No evidence has emerged of this endeavor.

Commander Michael “Gunshi” Allonois: Timbiqui is best known for its manufacture of beer and spirits. It should thus be of little surprise that the world’s planetary security has ties with the industry. As the vice-president of security at Timbiqui Spirits, Allonois rebuilt a personal Goliath, fueled—some say—by Timbiqui Dark. Salvage bought at a discount from the battlefields of St. Andre allowed the security force to expand into a militia, including several modified Goliaths. Allonois gained the nickname “Gunshi” (“Gun Shy” to his enemies) during a short mercenary contract. The Marik assaults of 3068 drew the militia into action. They held off the invaders for a week, beating back several units before negotiating an honorable surrender. Sadly, Allonois passed in 3071, eight years before the Alliance retook the world.:br::br:Colonel Fiona Yare Cochraine: Cochraine commanded the Fifth Capellan Chargers, better known as Cochraine’s Goliaths, when the unit was resurrected in 2990 with Goliaths from a Star League cache. She was a cunning commander who bridled under Chancellor Maximillian Liao’s restrictions against committing the heavy unit to battle. Cochraine believed her force’s formidable firepower could tip the balance of power in the ongoing conflict with the Federated Suns. During the attack on St. Andre in the Fourth Succession War, she and her force swiftly gained the upper hand against the invaders. A desperate counterattack by a Delta Company slowed the massed stalwart Goliaths. However, a suicidal death from above attack against her Goliath claimed her life. Without her leadership, morale crumbled, and the battalion was annihilated.:br::br:MechWarrior Mateo Alsahra’ Aleaqarib: Warriors from Nueva Castile are rare in the Inner Sphere, but some “Caballeros” entered service with Periphery states in the wake of the Clan invasion. Mateo Alsahra’ Aleaqarib never discussed what brought him to the Illyrian Palatinate in 3057, though there were suggestions of scandal and piracy. To the warriors of the Palatinate this was irrelevant. All that mattered was commitment to the Palatinate, something Aleaqarib demonstrated repeatedly in clashes with the Lothian League. While his venerable Goliath (rumored to be a “prize” captured from unknown Periphery forces) was far from cutting edge, his MechWarrior skills earned him the respect of his comrades, even if they found his mannerisms and attachment to the Goliath unusual.:br::br:Force Commander Edgardo Barag-Stone: BaragStone piloted a Goliath with the First Fusiliers of Oriente during Operation Bulldog in 3059. The First was decimated in the meat grinder of Marshdale. With many officers dead, the Marik unit neared collapse. Rather than flee, then-Lieutenant Barag-Stone rallied his company and executed a series of daring attacks to slow the Smoke Jaguar assaults. This bought time for the other Fusiliers to rally. Though badly wounded, his actions allowed the Fusiliers to escape the Clan troops. His courage earned him the Oriente Legion of Merit, bestowed by Duke Christopher Halas himself while Barag-Stone recuperated on Oriente. The duke invited him join the Ducal Guards. He accepted, rising to the rank of Force Commander before retiring in 3081, after the Jihad concluded.:br::br:Lieutenant Bhekampi Obote: Obote joined the Grey Death Legion after the bloodbath of Pandora. He quickly earned the respect and trust of his comrades and rose to command Second Company’s fire lance. Physically imposing like his Goliath—he stood nearly two meters tall—Obote’s quiet demeanor hid a dry sense of humor that he could use disarmingly. On the battlefield he was calm and efficient, providing precision fire support for the rest of the company. This was used to deadly effect in the Skye Rebellion of 3056. Obote’s fire lance proved so intimidating that eight enemy MechWarriors surrendered to his lance at Sheolport. Obote’s Goliath was destroyed in the battle at Lochaber Forest that lured so many Skye ’Mechs to their doom.:br::br:Kommandant Devian Azalin: Azalin was swept up in the fervor surrounding the formation of the Jaeger Regiments and joined the Skye Jaegers as the FedCom Civil War erupted. He participated in several engagements during the conflict and earned renown for his skillful Goliath piloting. The long range combat of the liberation of Hesperus II in 3074 cemented his reputation for marksmanship after a night-time combat drop helped drive off the Fortieth Shadow Division. Following the loss of many Jaeger officers, Azalin received a battlefield commission and later coordinated many of the Jaegers’ operations with ComStar’s Seventy-Ninth and 103rd Divisions in the Galatea campaign. He was promoted to kommandant, the rank he held until 3081, when—his long hair and ornate beard now grey rather than black—he retired.:br::br:Colonel Dwayne Bronson: Despite old ties to the noble Eridani Light Horse (whom he hated with a passion), the commander of Bronson’s Horde was an opportunist barely one step above a pirate. His fiery temperament was well-known, with outbursts sometimes moderated or fanned by his sister/XO, Robyn. A competent if unimaginative commander, he led the mercenary command from the cockpit of his Goliath. The Marian campaign of 3063 demonstrated his weather-vane politics, as he broke contract with the Hegemony and signed on with the Circinians. After being declared rogue in 3068, the Horde signed on with the Word of Blake and supported Shadow Division operations on New Avalon. Bronson’s Goliath fell to the Davion Assault Guards in August 3074. The few surviving Horde members scattered to the winds.:br::br:Cassandra “Cassie” Blue: Cassandra Blue grew up on the streets of Arcturus, spending time in juvenile correctional facilities for stealing LoaderMechs and participating in unlicensed street races. Her skill as a pilot was undeniable, but poor discipline made her ill-suited to a military career. She toured the Inner Sphere’s many informal IndustrialMech racing circuits, demonstrating her ability to push ’Mechs beyond their limits. Her skills caught the attention of Detroit Consolidated MechWorks. The Canopians made a simple offer: come test our ’Mechs—break them to make them better. The last dozen years have been a rollercoaster of wild rides (and sometimes extended hospital stays), but Blue has reveled in the adrenaline high. Given her hellion reputation, many of her colleagues would be surprised to learn of her hobby: restoring and souping up a classic Goliath.:br::br:Subaltern Murray “Dingo” Simmonds: Simmonds pilots a temperamental Goliath in a combined-arms Rapid Response Defense Company within the Taurian Concordat. He leads Dingo’s Wardogs, assigned to guard the border against Federated Suns’ and pirate incursions. Simmonds is a pragmatist, more interested in keeping his troops alive than in high ideals. He favors diplomacy, though if push comes to shove, his skilled, professional troops are capable of laying down withering barrages, and then redeploying before the  enemy can counter. While House Davion is the Concordat’s primary threat, Simmonds has a complicated relationship with a Davion colonel. Sometimes they cooperate in anti-pirate missions, and other times they fight. Unconfirmed rumors of another relationship, this one with the Davion colonel’s sister, would explain some of the friction between the pair.

The Goshawk II is a forty-five-ton Clan medium BattleMech developed by Clan Snow Raven in the mid-3080s, drawing inspiration from the heavier Vapor Eagle that the Ravens had long operated. Produced at Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on the Inner Sphere world of Dante, the Goshawk II was designed specifically as a second-line combat platform for exclusive use by Raven Alliance forces. Ten tons lighter than its progenitor, the Goshawk II compensates with significantly greater speed and agility, incorporating an ECM suite to counter the increasingly sophisticated electronic warfare capabilities encountered in Inner Sphere service. Clan Sea Fox later began producing their own variant at facilities in the Chain Cluster, expanding the design's availability beyond its original Raven Alliance exclusivity.

Built on a weight-saving GS-2E endo steel chassis, the Goshawk II mounts a 315-rated extralight fusion engine that pushes the forty-five-ton 'Mech to an impressive 118.8 km/h, substantially faster than the Vapor Eagle it descends from. Seven jump jets provide an equally impressive leap capability of two hundred and ten meters, exceeding even its larger ancestor's mobility. Nine tons of standard armor offer adequate protection for a design intended to operate at high speed, and an integral ECM suite helps neutralize the electronic warfare advantages that Inner Sphere opponents increasingly bring to the battlefield.

The Goshawk II's armament centers on a right-arm ER large laser as its sole long-range weapon, capable of engaging targets at significant distances with precision. Close-range firepower comes from a pair of small pulse lasers and six micro pulse lasers distributed across the arms and head, all guided by a targeting computer that maximizes their effectiveness. This energy-only configuration eliminates ammunition dependency, granting extended operational endurance well suited to the Raven Alliance's expeditionary doctrine. The design excels in high-speed slashing attacks, closing rapidly to deliver precise fire before withdrawing beyond effective retaliation range.

The Goshawk II's development reflects Clan Snow Raven's pragmatic approach to rebuilding their military strength following their relocation to the Outworlds Alliance. Having operated the larger Vapor Eagle since before the Clan Invasion, Raven engineers leveraged their deep familiarity with the design to produce a lighter, faster derivative better suited to their new operational reality as a Clan operating within the Inner Sphere. Production began at Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante in 3086, with the design designated exclusively for Raven second-line formations.

The Ravens' close commercial relationship with Clan Sea Fox eventually brought the design to wider distribution. Sea Fox merchants, recognizing the Goshawk II's export potential, began manufacturing their own variant at Manufacturing Plant SFF-AL1 on Alnabog in the Chain Cluster. This Sea Fox-produced Goshawk II 4 incorporated more advanced technology including an XXL engine, and was marketed to various buyers including the Republic of the Sphere.

The Republic's acquisition of Sea Fox-built Goshawk IIs led directly to the experimental RISC variant. In 3136, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat at their Sandhurst proving grounds on Terra attempted to install an experimental emergency coolant system into the platform. The project yielded only four converted test units before disastrous field trials ended the program. Three of four test units were destroyed within three months, including two from catastrophic coolant system failures that went undetected due to falsely reassuring temperature readouts. RISC shelved the project permanently, and Sea Fox component codes found on recovered wreckage successfully deflected media scrutiny away from the Republic's covert involvement.

The Götterdämmerung is a seventy-five-ton heavy BattleMech first fielded by the Lyran Commonwealth in 3138. Designed by Blackstone BattleMechs on Inarcs, the ’Mech (whose German name translates to “Twilight of the Gods”) was explicitly intended as a modern replacement for the ancient Thunderbolt. Blackstone drew upon lessons learned from over six centuries of Thunderbolt service to create a design that prioritized survivability above all else, incorporating a torso-mounted cockpit, compact engine, and heavy ferro-fibrous armor.

The Götterdämmerung quickly earned a mixed reputation upon entering service. Its durability became legendary, making it a common sight in half a dozen LCAF frontline regiments and numerous mercenary commands. However, its complex ejection system made the ’Mech notoriously difficult to escape from when downed, a trade-off that MechWarriors have regarded with understandable ambivalence.

The Götterdämmerung’s remarkable survivability stems from multiple complementary design choices. Layers of StarSlab/4 heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide exceptional protection per ton, while the Blackstone ETG Endo Steel chassis saves weight for additional systems. The Edasich 300 compact fusion engine and compact gyro occupy less critical internal volume than standard equivalents, meaning that even severe structural damage is less likely to disable the ’Mech’s motive systems. This combination gives the Götterdämmerung the same sixty-four kilometer per hour top speed as its Thunderbolt predecessor while being substantially harder to put down.

Offensively, a Defiance 1001 extended-range PPC in the right arm provides the primary long-range punch. A Coventry StarFire LRM-15 launcher is mounted in the head, an unusual placement that keeps the ammunition in the most protected location on the chassis. Five Defiance Model XII extended-range medium lasers clustered in the center torso deliver devastating close-range firepower that is extremely difficult for an opponent to neutralize without a center torso kill. The torso-mounted cockpit enhances pilot protection but introduces a complex ejection sequence involving retractable combat shrouds and explosive bolts, making escape from a downed Götterdämmerung a harrowing prospect. MechWarriors must also guard against losing side torsos, as the life support systems are split between them.

Blackstone BattleMechs introduced the Götterdämmerung in 3138 from their facilities on Inarcs, entering a market long dominated by the venerable Thunderbolt. The design was conceived specifically to succeed the aging T-Bolt in Lyran Commonwealth service, and Blackstone’s engineers incorporated every survivability enhancement available to ensure the new chassis would live up to its predecessor’s legendary toughness.

The Götterdämmerung’s reputation was cemented during the Nineteenth Battle of Hesperus II, where the Schachtebich Jägers’ Götterdämmerung units demonstrated extraordinary resilience against Clan Wolf opponents. In one notable engagement in the Sulden Uplands of North Whitman, a Jäger Götterdämmerung engaged multiple Clan Wolf ’Mechs, absorbing catastrophic damage. It lost its head, left arm, left torso, and three of its medium lasers, yet continued fighting. Even with its offensive capability severely degraded, the ’Mech managed to eliminate a Point of battle armor before a second Point finally brought it down. This performance so impressed Clan Sea Fox’s Tiburon Khanate that they began selling upgrade kits consisting of Clan-grade weapons and Ferro-Lamellor armor to mercenary units with sufficient funds.

The Götterdämmerung has since become a fixture in LCAF frontline regiments and among well-funded mercenary commands. Rumors persist that the Tiburon Khanate is exploring the possibility of a full factory-produced Clan-tech variant, which would represent a significant evolution of Blackstone’s original design philosophy.

The Griffin is one of the oldest BattleMech designs still in active service, with origins stretching back over six centuries. Originally conceived by Maxwell Manufacturing, Inc. on Procyon as a sixty-ton heavy 'Mech for the Hegemony Armed Forces, the prototype GRF-1A first walked in 2465 and entered full production by 2492. Earthwerks Incorporated later acquired and overhauled the design into the lighter, faster fifty-five-ton GRF-1N that became the definitive Griffin. Reclassified as a medium fire support platform, the Griffin proved enormously popular with commanders and pilots across the Inner Sphere. Licensed production across numerous manufacturers ensured the design survived the devastation of the Succession Wars largely intact. Built by the tens of thousands, the Griffin has served continuously through the Age of War, the Succession Wars, the Clan Invasion, the Jihad, and into the ilClan era.

The Griffin's enduring success rests on a simple but effective combination of long-range firepower and battlefield mobility. The standard GRF-1N mounts a Fusigon PPC in a detachable right-arm housing paired with a Delta Dart LRM-10 launcher in a drum over the right shoulder, giving the design both direct and indirect fire support capability. A CoreTek 275 fusion engine drives the chassis to a top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour, while five Rawlings 55 jump jets provide a hundred and fifty meters of jumping distance, a combination that allows the Griffin to dictate engagement range against most opponents.

This firepower comes with notable compromises. All weapons are concentrated on the right side of the chassis, creating a critical vulnerability if that flank is compromised. The design also lacks any short-range defensive armament, leaving Griffin pilots dangerously exposed when enemies close to knife-fighting range. Nine and a half tons of Starshield A armor compares favorably to many medium 'Mechs, though the Griffin frequently faces heavier opponents. Twelve single heat sinks prove insufficient for sustained fire, forcing pilots to choose between engaging and withdrawing rather than doing both simultaneously. The design's forgiving heat curve at walking speeds partially mitigates this limitation during disciplined long-range engagements.

The Griffin's history begins with Maxwell Manufacturing's successful bid to produce a highly mobile BattleMech for the Hegemony Armed Forces. The original sixty-ton GRF-1A quickly earned a prominent role in HAF assault battalions, remaining on front lines even as newer designs superseded it. Maxwell's dissolution due to corporate misconduct in the late twenty-fifth century transferred the design to Earthwerks Incorporated, who overhauled it into the fifty-five-ton GRF-1N, lighter, faster, with greater jump capacity and a more powerful missile launcher. This reclassified medium 'Mech became one of the most widely produced BattleMechs in history.

Production spread across the Inner Sphere through licensing agreements with Defiance Industries on Hesperus II, Kallon Industries on Talon, Brigadier Corporation on Oliver, and Norse BattleMech Works on Marduk. Vandenberg Mechanized Industries even manufactured the design in the Periphery on Illiushin. Only the Capellan Confederation lacked domestic production capability, purchasing limited numbers from the Taurian Concordat. By 2857, Defiance Industries had introduced the GRF-1S, the first production variant, reconfiguring the design as a medium-range brawler for the Lyran Commonwealth.

The Fourth Succession War reshuffled production lines when the Draconis Combine captured Marduk from the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth took Oliver from the Free Worlds League. This coincided with the rediscovery of lostech, spawning new variants that quickly spread beyond their intended factions. The Clan Invasion accelerated this trend, with manufacturers rushing upgraded designs into production. Vicore Industries' Project Phoenix initiative prompted Defiance and Kallon to produce the completely redesigned GRF-6S, while Victory Industries joined after acquiring light fusion engine technology. The Free Worlds League and ComStar each developed their own updates, with ComStar's variant ominously appearing in Word of Blake Militia ranks.

The Jihad saw the Griffin deployed on all sides of the conflict, with the Word of Blake fielding the deadly GRF-4R refit and the Capellan Confederation finally fielding indigenous variants incorporating stealth armor. Following the Jihad, Brigadier Corporation introduced the advanced GRF-6R, and production continued within the Free Worlds League at Earthwerks' facilities. The Wolf Empire's conquest of Terra brought further evolution as Earthwerks' Keystone plant began producing the Griffin C, a Clan-specification refit of older models using captured Clan weapons technology. Spread across the Inner Sphere by Clan Sea Fox traders, the Griffin C ensured the venerable design remained competitive into the ilClan era. Notable engagements throughout this long history include the War Griffins mercenary cadre's exclusive use of the chassis during the Second Succession War, pirate-hunting operations on Hazeldean, and distinguished service during the siege of Odin Manufacturing Works on Orestes during the Second Combine-Dominion War.

shared: The Grigori is the lighter of two heavy Celestial OmniMechs produced by the Word of Blake for its Manei Domini forces. Named after the fallen angels of Christian tradition, the sixty-ton design was the last of the six Celestials to reach production, entering service in late 3069 after Doctor Devon Cortland personally supervised its final manufacturing run at Sekkaris Mekwerks on Mars. Gibson Federated BattleMechs and Martinson Armaments manufactured the design at facilities on Gibson and Terra. Intended to pair with the seventy-ton Deva in heavy Level IIs, the Grigori provides layered missile fire support that complements its heavier sibling's direct engagement role.

The Grigori is built on a Celestial Series GG1 standard chassis powered by a GM 240 light fusion engine, giving it a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. An XL gyro and small cockpit reduce internal volume requirements, while eleven tons of Divine Shield-B light ferro-fibrous armor provide above-average protection for a sixty-ton design. Twenty-eight tons of pod space give the Grigori exceptional configuration flexibility for its weight class, approaching the capacity of many heavier OmniMechs. A fixed C3i computer links it into the networked targeting systems shared by all Celestial designs, enabling coordinated fire missions across the formation.

Unlike the other Celestials, the Grigori's Invictus configuration is primarily a missile platform, mounting an MRM-20, LRM-15, and Streak SRM-4 for layered firepower across all range brackets. A light PPC and retractable blade provide backup when ammunition runs low. Other configurations shift toward energy-heavy loadouts with heavy PPCs, jump capability, and electronic warfare suites, demonstrating the versatility afforded by the generous pod allocation.

The Grigori's delayed entry into production reflected Doctor Devon Cortland's perfectionism rather than any engineering setback. Cortland had conceived all six Celestial OmniMechs as an integrated combat system at the Sekkaris Mekwerks facility on Mars, each design filling a specific tactical niche within Manei Domini formations. The Grigori represented the final piece of that system, and Cortland refused to release the design until its missile-heavy Invictus configuration met his exacting standards. His personal supervision of the final manufacturing run at Sekkaris delayed the Grigori by several weeks relative to its siblings, but ensured the design performed exactly as intended when it finally reached the Shadow Divisions.

Cortland's design philosophy treated the Grigori and Deva as halves of a single tactical concept. Where other militaries designed heavy 'Mechs as generalist platforms, Cortland created two specialized complements: the Grigori to saturate targets at range with missile fire, the Deva to close and destroy them with direct energy and ballistic weapons. The C3i network was the glue binding the two together. A Grigori could feed targeting solutions to an advancing Deva, adjusting fire in real time as the heavier design maneuvered into position. Conversely, Deva pilots pushing forward could relay sensor data back to supporting Grigoris, allowing indirect missile fire against targets the fire support 'Mech could not see directly. This complementary doctrine was among the most sophisticated paired-unit tactics the Inner Sphere had seen since the fall of the Star League.

The Forty-seventh Shadow Division, known as "Azazel's Watchers," deployed Grigoris extensively in combined-arms formations where their missile configurations saturated enemy positions with coordinated volleys. Poltergeist Precentor Sigma Tamiel of the Forty-seventh piloted a custom Grigori equipped with dual Thunderbolt 10 launchers and a snub-nose PPC, combining precision guided munitions with direct fire. His configuration also incorporated jump jets and a Guardian ECM suite, reflecting the tactical flexibility that commanders demanded from their personal machines.

Senior Manei Domini officers viewed the Grigori's generous pod space as an ideal platform for personalized loadouts. Demi-Precentor Rufus of the Opacus Venatori operated another custom configuration tailored for independent operations, and the design saw proportionally more custom work than lighter Celestials where pod constraints limited experimentation. The Exanimus underwater variant demonstrated the Grigori's adaptability further, equipping it with underwater maneuvering units and direct-fire energy weapons rather than the torpedoes most underwater designs relied on, a choice that reflected the Manei Domini preference for ammunition-independent firepower.

Surviving Grigoris are among the rarer Celestial sightings in the post-Jihad era. Their larger size made them more difficult to conceal than the lighter Malak and Preta, and their value depended heavily on pairing with a Deva, a combination that remnant cells struggle to maintain. Republic intelligence occasionally documented Grigori encounters during anti-remnant operations through the 3080s and 3090s, typically associated with fortified holdout positions where the design's fire support capabilities could be employed from prepared firing positions. The Caelestis variant, mounting captured Clan streak missile launchers and pulse lasers, represented the pinnacle of Grigori development and demonstrated that even a fire support platform could become a devastating brawler with the right configuration.

text.overview:
Electronic warfare underwent a technical revolution with the arrival of the Clans, as BattleMech sensor capabilities once again rivaled and often surpassed those of the best Star League-era units. In the wake of the liberation of Hesperus II from the Word of Blake, the Lyran Alliance made the development of a dedicated electronic warfare reconnaissance unit a top priority. Utilizing cutting-edge detection and anti-detection technologies, Lyran engineers created the Ghost in 3077, a fifty-ton medium strike 'Mech designed to complement the Griffin in hunter-killer and heavy raiding operations.

Help from the Duchy of Oriente's Earthwerks-FWL, Incorporated established a second production line on Calloway VI, creating an unusual cross-border partnership. The high cost of stealth components and ongoing legal disputes over the technology have kept production runs relatively small, though both manufacturers offer a simplified variant for open-market purchase.
text.capabilities:
The Ghost is designed around its stealth armor capabilities, many of which were pioneered with the Mongoose II design. Ten and a half tons of Starshield Ultra-Tech stealth armor, powered by a Guardian ECM suite integrated into the Nashan communications system, allow the Ghost to approach targets virtually undetected. A Beagle active probe mounted alongside the Nashan Trac V-102 targeting system provides exceptional detection capabilities, enabling the 'Mech to identify hidden units and defeat enemy electronic countermeasures.

Powered by a GM 300 XL engine, the Ghost achieves a top speed approaching one hundred kilometers per hour, placing it among the fastest medium 'Mechs in its weight class. Twin Defiance 1002 light particle projector cannons deliver solid damage at respectable ranges, while two Helga Series multi-missile launcher three-packs provide flexible fire support with both long-range and short-range missile loadouts. A BlazeFire Longshot extended-range medium laser serves as a versatile close-range auxiliary weapon.

While the Ghost does not carry overwhelming firepower, fourteen double heat sinks ensure it can maintain a punishing rate of fire throughout an engagement. The combination of speed, stealth, and electronic warfare systems makes it a fearsome deep penetration raider, capable of dictating the pace and range of any encounter.
text.deployment: This custom arena configuration debuted in 3144 on the Tennessee Valley Arena circuit. The most striking modification is the replacement of the original stealth armor with Clan-specification ferro-fibrous armor and the addition of a Void Signature System, providing a fundamentally different approach to battlefield concealment. The weapons suite has been extensively reworked, with the light particle projector cannons giving way to three extended-range medium lasers and an extended-range small pulse laser, while a single MML-9 replaces the twin MML-3 launchers. An improved Narc missile beacon dispensing Haywire pods rounds out the electronic warfare package in place of the original Beagle active probe.
text.battleHistory:
The Ghost's development began in the closing stages of the Jihad, when the liberation of Hesperus II from the Word of Blake made the creation of a dedicated electronic warfare reconnaissance unit a Lyran Alliance priority. The design process proved arduous and logistically nightmarish, requiring engineers to corral cutting-edge components from across a fractured Inner Sphere while simultaneously repairing Defiance Industries' war-damaged facilities on Hesperus II.

An unlikely partnership emerged when the Duchy of Oriente's Earthwerks-FWL, Incorporated reached out to offer aid. In exchange for the rights to produce the Ghost in their own factories, Earthwerks helped the Lyran Alliance acquire and ship the needed parts and labor to finish both the prototype and the main Defiance production line. This symbiotic relationship resulted in all Earthwerks-manufactured Ghosts featuring Lyran power plants, an unusual cross-border supply chain that persisted well beyond the Jihad.

The Royal Guards regiments of the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces were the first units to receive production Ghosts, and the design quickly became a favorite among Lyran commanders for its ability to disrupt enemy supply lines and command structures. In the Oriente Protectorate, the Ghost was assigned to elite reconnaissance companies within the Fusiliers regiments, where its stealth capabilities proved well-suited to intelligence-gathering operations along contested borders.

Technological limitations surrounding the construction of stealth armor, combined with an expected but ugly legal battle with manufacturers in the Capellan Confederation over the technology, kept production runs small throughout the design's early history. Both Defiance Industries and Earthwerks offered the simplified GST-11 for open-market sale in an effort to offset the high production costs, and the variant began appearing in military units across the Inner Sphere. Select mercenary commands expressed interest in the Ghost, though fielding one remained a rarity given the limited numbers available.

By the mid-3080s, Earthwerks undertook an ambitious redesign that produced the GST-50, rebuilding the 'Mech from the ground up with more affordable components to broaden its market appeal. The disruption of Gray Monday in 3133 further drove innovation, as operators began field-modifying the GST-50 with industrial chainsaws to exploit the variant's sensor signature resemblance to civilian Crosscut LoggerMechs, adding a deceptive edge to an already stealthy lineage.

text.deployment: The only documented variant of the original Goliath was an attempt to increase the 'Mech's armor past 18 tons by dropping four heat sinks. Ultimately, the torsos were already armored to their structural maximum, so the machine guns were replaced by a third LRM launcher to create this variant. The result trades anti-infantry capability for additional long-range missile firepower, making it a more dedicated fire-support platform.

One of the 'new generation' of Goliaths, the 3S's engine has been upgraded to a Light Fusion Engine, and, as a result, it now carries thirteen and a half tons of armor. The entire arsenal has been stripped from the 'Mech and the 3S carries as its primary weapon an LB-X Autocannon/20. This is backed up by three ER Medium Lasers. For longer-range engagements, the Goliath carries an LRM-10 launcher with an Artemis IV fire control system as well as an ER Large Laser.

Produced by Clan Sea Fox at their Alnabog facility in the Chain Cluster, the Goshawk II 4 stands as a significant departure from the Snow Raven-designed originals. Powered by a hotter-running XXL engine, this variant mounts an improved heavy large laser, a Streak LRM-10 for guided long-range fire, and a plasma cannon for engaging both BattleMechs and conventional vehicles. Despite carrying twelve double heat sinks, the combination of the XXL engine and energy-intensive weapons creates persistent heat management challenges that have made this variant especially unpopular with pilots. The Goshawk II 4 was marketed to various Inner Sphere buyers, including the Republic of the Sphere.

production.manufacturer: Refit - Republic Institute of Strategic Combat Proving Ground Egalité

text.deployment: Designated the Goshawk II RISC, this experimental variant was created in 3136 by the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat using Sea Fox-sourced Goshawk II 4 airframes. RISC engineers attempted to address the base variant's heat management problems by installing an experimental emergency coolant system, but this required removing a heat sink from the already thermally challenged design. While the ECS performed well in controlled testing, live-fire trials proved catastrophic. Three of four test units were destroyed within three months, two from explosive ruptures in the coolant lines that went undetected as the ECS initially masked rising temperatures behind reassuring readouts. The project was permanently shelved, and Sea Fox component markings on recovered wreckage successfully obscured the Republic's involvement.

Following the impressive performance of a Schachtebich Jägers Götterdämmerung during the Nineteenth Battle of Hesperus II, Clan Sea Fox’s Tiburon Khanate began selling upgrade kits for the design. The GTD-20C replaces the standard weapons and armor with Clan-grade equivalents of the existing loadout, while substituting Ferro-Lamellor armor for the original heavy ferro-fibrous plating. This provides dramatically improved protection against both ballistic and energy weapons. The upgrade is marketed primarily to mercenary units with sufficient funds, and rumors persist that the Khanate is exploring the possibility of a full factory-production model rather than limiting availability to upgrade kits.

A factory variant offered by Blackstone BattleMechs alongside the standard GTD-20S, the GTD-30S draws inspiration from modern Thunderbolt variants to modify the base design’s engagement profile. The head-mounted LRM-15 is exchanged for an SRM-6 launcher, shifting the secondary weapons capability from long-range indirect fire to close-range brawling. The five ER medium lasers give way to three medium pulse lasers and an ER flamer, improving accuracy at close range while adding an anti-infantry and heat-building capability. This configuration transforms the Götterdämmerung from a versatile all-range combatant into a more focused close-quarters assault platform.

text.overview: The Dragon and later Grand Dragon have been a staple of Draconis Combine cavalry units since the early days of the Succession Wars. Attempts by LAW to modernize this emblematic BattleMech over the past century largely met with success and never strayed from the basic performance profile. LAW wisely chose to keep with tradition in this latest variant, while taking advantage of the influx of Clan-grade weaponry. In order to reduce costs, many components are shared with the newest Lancelot variant. The resulting DRG-12K is far and away the most deadly Grand Dragon to enter DCMS rolls.
text.notableUnits: Tai-i Ryouji Kurashige: Kurashige served with honor and distinction during the Combine’s early campaigns against the Republic of the Sphere in the wake of Gray Monday. His commanders viewed him as a model warrior and as a creative leader and tactician. Kurashige’s request to undergo DEST training was quickly approved. He excelled there despite his preference for BattleMech-centric operations compared to stealthier battlesuit missions. Kurashige’s fervent loyalty to both the Combine and Coordinator Yori was rewarded when the Coordinator quietly formed the Hikage. Kurashige was selected to lead a company of the new Dragon’s Shadow. From the cockpit of his black and red Grand Dragon, Tai-i Kurashige continues his lifelong service to the Draconis Combine.

text.overview: The Grand Summoner is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 3093 by Clan Jade Falcon as a direct replacement for the venerable Summoner. Produced by the Eagle Craft Group at their facility on Erewhon, the Grand Summoner was designed to address the aging Summoner's limitations while preserving the proven mobility and firepower balance that had made its predecessor a mainstay of Clan heavy cavalry formations for over two centuries. The design quickly spread beyond its Jade Falcon origins through inter-Clan trade, finding particular favor among the Inner Sphere Clans' warrior castes. Known to Inner Sphere intelligence services by the reporting name Thor II, the Grand Summoner has established itself as a reliable and versatile frontline OmniMech favored by junior grade officers for independent operations.
text.capabilities:
The Grand Summoner retains the same Magna 350 XL engine as its predecessor, maintaining the same top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour that made the original Summoner effective in fast-moving engagements. The critical improvement lies in the adoption of an Olivetti T4 Endo Steel internal structure combined with the conversion of the Summoner's fixed jump jets to pod-mounted equipment, freeing thirty and a half tons of pod space compared to the original's twenty-two and a half. Compound Beta ferro-fibrous armor provides marginally better protection than the original Summoner, adding half a ton of additional coverage across the design.

The Grand Summoner's Model J-D 067 communications system is a standout feature that has elevated the design beyond a simple heavy cavalry platform. Capable of supporting three times the number of simultaneous connections compared to competing systems such as the Alpha-com, the 067 can also cut through standard ECM interference when operating at maximum power, making the Grand Summoner a natural command platform despite not being originally intended for that role. The Hawkeye 58 targeting and tracking system, while highly accurate, requires recalibration whenever the OmniMech's pod configuration is changed, briefly leaving the 'Mech unable to employ its weapons during the process.
text.deployment: Alternate Configuration E exploits the Grand Summoner's generous pod space to mount eight improved jump jets, granting a remarkable two-hundred-forty-meter jump radius that rivals many light 'Mechs. This extraordinary mobility is paired with a straightforward all-energy weapons loadout consisting of an ER PPC in each arm and an ER small laser in the center torso, ensuring the E configuration is never dependent on ammunition supplies. Two additional double heat sinks help manage the thermal load from sustained PPC fire. The E configuration is ideally suited for reconnaissance-in-force missions and flanking maneuvers across broken terrain where its jump capability allows it to reach positions that heavier opponents cannot follow.
text.battleHistory:
The Grand Summoner emerged from Clan Jade Falcon's recognition that the Summoner, while still serviceable, was showing its age after more than two centuries of continuous production. The Eagle Craft Group's Erewhon facility began production in 3093, and the Jade Falcons treated the new design as a symbol of Clan pride from its very first chassis. The inaugural Grand Summoner, bearing serial number JF000-01A, was mounted on a ceremonial dais at the Erewhon factory complex gate rather than being deployed to a frontline unit. Each year, the Jade Falcon Khan selects one Cluster to be honored for distinguished service, and JF000-01A is repainted in that Cluster's parade colors. The Third Falcon Talon Cluster holds the distinction of being selected five times, more than any other formation.

The design's proliferation beyond Clan Jade Falcon came through the inter-Clan trade networks that characterized the post-Jihad era. Other Inner Sphere Clans readily adopted the Grand Summoner, recognizing its advantages over the original Summoner design. Though the largest concentrations of Grand Summoners remained within the Jade Falcon touman, the design became a common sight in the formations of allied and rival Clans alike.

One of the Grand Summoner's most celebrated engagements occurred on Feltre in 3097, when Clan Wolf Star Colonel Jess Calvert challenged Clan Diamond Shark's Swimmer Khanate to a Trial of Possession for the entire Beta Aimag. Aggressive bidding reduced each side's forces to a single Cluster. The Diamond Sharks selected the Swordtooth Canyons as the trial grounds, a labyrinth of ravines, dead ends, and heavy electromagnetic interference that degraded communications and tracking systems. The fighting quickly devolved into small-unit actions where the Grand Summoner's superior communications suite proved decisive, allowing Diamond Shark Stars to maintain coordination while Wolf forces struggled with disrupted signals. The Diamond Sharks' victory in this trial cemented the Grand Summoner's reputation as a design that could turn difficult terrain from a liability into an advantage.

text.overview: The Grasshopper entered service in 2780 as a heavy close-range BattleMech designed for the Star League Defense Force. Originally conceived as a stealthy hunter-killer of light and medium 'Mechs, difficulties integrating experimental stealth systems with the chassis delayed the design past the end of the Amaris Civil War, and the troublesome technology was ultimately stripped from the final production model. The untested and unorthodox 'Mech was distributed throughout the Regular Army rather than the more prestigious Royal divisions, and within four years Grasshoppers could be found in most SLDF regiments. As the Star League dissolved, the chaos of Operation EXODUS and the defection of SLDF units carried the design into virtually every Successor State army. Manufactured by Lantren Corporation on Bryant, the Grasshopper earned an enduring reputation as a mobile, self-reliant heavy 'Mech capable of operating far from established supply lines, and its rugged construction kept the design on battlefields for centuries despite severely limited production numbers.
text.capabilities:
The Grasshopper combines heavy 'Mech firepower with mobility typically associated with lighter designs. Its VOX 280 engine provides a ground speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, while four Leviathon Lifter jump jets grant a jump capability of one hundred and twenty meters—remarkable for a seventy-ton chassis. This combination allows the Grasshopper to close rapidly with enemy formations, appearing suddenly in the midst of tightly-packed units where its predominantly short-ranged armament is most devastating.

The primary weapon, a Diplan HD large laser mounted in the center torso, ensures the Grasshopper remains combat-capable even after suffering crippling limb damage, earning it the classification of a "zombie" 'Mech among field commanders. Four Diplan M3 medium lasers spread across the torso and arms allow return fire from virtually any angle, while a single Conan/S LRM-5 provides token long-range harassment primarily used to soften targets before the lasers come to bear. Twenty-two heat sinks give the design superior thermal management compared to other heavy 'Mechs, and its near-exclusive reliance on energy weapons frees it from ammunition dependency—a critical advantage during extended independent operations.

Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection for the design's weight class, though the Grasshopper can be outgunned by dedicated fire-support platforms of similar tonnage. The design philosophy accepts this trade-off, relying instead on mobility and endurance to dictate the terms of engagement.
text.deployment: The GHR-5S is a minor modification of the original Grasshopper design, replacing the head-mounted LRM-5 launcher with an SRM-4 rack. This straightforward exchange trades the limited long-range harassment capability for improved close-range punch, better suiting the Grasshopper's preferred engagement envelope where its laser armament is most effective. The modification was simple enough to be performed in the field and saw scattered adoption across multiple armies during the Succession Wars.
text.battleHistory:
The Grasshopper's history is inextricably linked to the fall of the Star League. Designed by Lantren Corporation on Bryant for the SLDF, the 'Mech entered service in 2780—too late for the Amaris Civil War it was originally intended to fight in. Problems integrating experimental stealth systems had delayed production by years, and when those systems were ultimately abandoned, the resulting conventional design was distributed to Regular Army formations rather than the elite Royal divisions. This widespread distribution proved fateful; as the Star League dissolved and SLDF units defected to the Successor States during Operation EXODUS, Grasshoppers were carried into virtually every House army.

The First Succession War proved the crucible that forged the Grasshopper's reputation. Its mobility and endurance made it a premier 'Mech for storming fortifications, and it frequently spearheaded assaults that exploited its jump capability to bypass defensive positions. The Grasshopper also served effectively as a backup brawler in companies of light and medium 'Mechs, and its self-reliance made it prized by mercenary commands. However, the design remained an uncommon sight during the Succession Wars, causing many commanders to mistakenly treat it as just another heavy 'Mech until it leapt into their midst and disrupted their formations. ComStar's publication of Technical Readout: 3025 finally brought wider awareness of the Grasshopper's true capabilities.

The Second Succession War dealt a severe blow to production when the Lantren Corporation factory on Bryant was destroyed in 2843 by a Free Worlds League raiding force that damaged the facility's protective domes, exposing it to the planet's worsening global storms. New production ceased entirely for over two centuries. Despite this, the Grasshopper's rugged construction meant that most of the original production run survived through careful maintenance, with many units prioritizing Grasshopper repairs over even a commander's personal 'Mech.

The technological renaissance of the thirty-first century breathed new life into the design. Lantren Corporation introduced the GHR-5J upgrade in 3049, incorporating recovered Star League technology, though the original 5H remained so popular it outnumbered the upgrade three to one for decades. Only when the Draconis Combine introduced its C3-equipped variants did this trend begin to reverse. LexaTech Industries of Hun Ho recognized the growing demand and began production of the completely redesigned GHR-6K in 3064, establishing a new production line that would generate several further variants including the Jihad-era GHR-7K. Jalastar Aerospace on Panpour later secured a license to produce the 6K for the Federated Suns.

During the Jihad, Arc-Royal MechWorks developed experimental prototypes incorporating cutting-edge technology, eventually producing the refined GHR-7P in 3081 primarily for the mercenary market. Rumors also circulated that the Word of Blake had reopened the original Lantren factory on Bryant, supported by higher-than-expected concentrations of Grasshoppers observed in Blakist forces. The Grasshopper has continued to serve across every major conflict of the thirty-first century and beyond, with LexaTech's GHR-8K representing the design's continued evolution in the ilClan era.

text.deployment: This customized Griffin carries modifications tailored to its pilot's preferred combat style. The specific technical alterations optimize the standard 1DS platform for particular tactical situations, reflecting the kind of personal modifications that experienced MechWarriors often demand from their maintenance crews. Like many named variants, this configuration is a one-off field modification rather than a production model.

Produced for the Free Worlds League, this variant trades the standard PPC for a medium laser while doubling the missile launcher capacity to an LRM-20. This reconfiguration shifts the Griffin from a direct-fire platform to a dedicated missile support chassis, dramatically increasing its indirect fire capability at the cost of sustained energy weapon engagement range. The variant proved influential within Marik military doctrine and provided direct inspiration for several upgraded models developed during the technological renaissance of the 3050s.

A Clan Invasion-era update of the throne room guard concept, this variant retains the close-quarters defensive focus of the GRF-1RG while incorporating pulse laser technology. The right-arm medium laser is retained, but the remaining lasers are upgraded to pulse variants, including a large pulse laser, two medium pulse lasers, and two small pulse lasers. One ton of machine gun ammunition was removed and three heat sinks dropped, though the remaining heat sinks were upgraded to double-strength models to partially compensate. The result is a dramatically more accurate close-range combatant suited to the confined spaces and rapid engagement timelines of its original guard role.

Introduced after the Jihad by Brigadier Corporation, this variant serves as a departure from the Griffin's traditional energy-weapon primary armament. A rotary autocannon/2 in the right arm provides a high volume of ballistic fire, supported by a Thunderbolt 10 missile launcher in the right torso. Two tons of rotary autocannon ammunition and three tons of Thunderbolt missiles provide reasonable endurance, while an ER small laser and Guardian ECM suite round out the loadout. Powered by an XL engine, this variant trades the Griffin's characteristic PPC for sustained rapid-fire capability that proves particularly effective against light armor and infantry formations.

production.manufacturer: Defiance Industries, Kallon Industries, Victory Industries

text.deployment: The Invictus configuration is unique among the Celestials for its missile-heavy primary loadout. An MRM-20, LRM-15, and Streak SRM-4 provide layered firepower across all range brackets, allowing the Grigori to engage targets from maximum range through close combat. A light PPC and retractable blade serve as backup when ammunition runs low. CASE protects the four tons of concentrated ammunition storage. The configuration leverages the C3i network to deliver coordinated missile salvos with devastating accuracy.

The Dominus configuration shifts the Grigori toward direct-fire combat. A heavy PPC serves as the primary weapon, delivering damage equal to Clan-grade particle cannons. Paired ER medium lasers and medium pulse lasers provide close-range firepower, while a head-mounted Streak SRM-6 adds a reliable finishing blow. Four jump jets enable leaps of one hundred twenty meters, and two extra double heat sinks manage thermal buildup. CASE protects the missile ammunition from catastrophic detonation.

The Infernus configuration maintains the Grigori's missile-centric identity while adding versatility. Artemis IV-guided MML-7 launchers in each arm fire both long and short-range munitions with enhanced accuracy. A plasma rifle provides devastating anti-infantry and anti-vehicle firepower, supplemented by a medium pulse laser and rear-mounted ER small laser. Four jump jets preserve tactical mobility. CASE protects the ammunition bins from sympathetic detonation, a critical concern given the mixed munitions carried.

The Comminus configuration combines electronic warfare with saturated missile fire. Three MRM-10 launchers exploit the C3i network for improved accuracy, while twin Streak SRM-6 launchers spread damage across enemy targets. A Guardian ECM suite provides electronic screening for the formation, and two ER medium lasers offer ammunition-independent backup. Jump jets enable the Grigori to maintain advantageous firing positions. CASE protects the substantial ammunition reserves required by the missile-heavy loadout.

The Luminos configuration transforms the Grigori into a highly mobile sniper. Six improved jump jets enable leaps of one hundred eighty meters, far exceeding standard configurations. A heavy PPC and light PPC provide devastating ranged firepower, while two ER medium lasers and a pair of ER small lasers defend against enemies who close inside minimum PPC range. The configuration sacrifices the Grigori's signature missile capability for unmatched battlefield positioning and long-range precision.

The Eminus configuration mounts an experimental Thunderbolt 15 missile launcher that delivers a concentrated warhead against single targets, supported by two tons of ammunition. An ER PPC provides sustained ranged firepower, while five ER medium lasers and an ER small laser deliver punishing close-range volleys. Two extra double heat sinks and CASE complete the package. The configuration serves as a proving ground for experimental weapon systems while maintaining credible combat effectiveness across all engagement ranges.

The Caelestis is an experimental configuration incorporating advanced and captured Clan-sourced technology. Fielded in limited numbers by select Shadow Division units, it demonstrates the Word of Blake's willingness to integrate experimental weapon systems into front-line combat platforms. The loadout pushes the boundaries of what Inner Sphere technology can achieve within the Grigori's generous twenty-eight-ton pod capacity, combining weapons and equipment unavailable to other factions during the Jihad.

The Exanimus configuration adapts the Grigori for underwater and unusual environment operations. A quartet of underwater maneuvering units provide subsurface mobility, while the weapon loadout is optimized for engagements in aquatic and zero-gravity environments. The configuration enables the Grigori to defend submerged installations and conduct amphibious operations, a capability that proved valuable for protecting critical Blakist infrastructure during the Jihad. Modified sensors compensate for the reduced effectiveness of standard targeting systems underwater.

text.overview:
The Guillotine was first designed in 2499 by Newhart Industries as a heavy shock unit for the Terran Hegemony, quickly establishing itself as one of the most reliable seventy-ton BattleMechs in the Star League Defense Force. Built to deliver devastating close-range firepower while maintaining exceptional mobility for its weight class, the Guillotine became a mainstay of SLDF heavy regiments for generations. As the march of technology produced heavier and more powerful designs, the Guillotine gradually transitioned from a front-line assault role to that of a heavy raider and harassment unit, a mission profile its speed, jump capability, and energy-heavy weapons suite made it ideally suited for.

The destruction of Newhart's New Earth factory during the Amaris Civil War in 2776 dealt a severe blow to production, though Irian BattleMechs Unlimited continued to manufacture the design under license from their facility on Irian. The technological decline of the Succession Wars forced a downgrade to the simpler GLT-4L model, but the recovery of the Helm Memory Core in the late 3040s enabled Irian to restore and ultimately surpass the original design's capabilities, ensuring the Guillotine's continued service well into the thirty-second century.
text.capabilities:
The Guillotine achieves an impressive balance of firepower, protection, and mobility for a seventy-ton heavy 'Mech. Its VOX 280 engine drives the chassis to a respectable sixty-four kilometers per hour, while four Anderson 398 jump jets provide a 120-meter jump capability that allows it to exploit difficult terrain such as mountains and jungles where heavier designs cannot follow. Twelve tons of Ulston Prime armor offer protection comparable to many assault-class machines, enabling the Guillotine to absorb considerable punishment during its characteristic aggressive engagements.

The primary armament centers on a Sunglow Type 2 large laser in the left arm, backed by four ExoStar II medium lasers distributed across the arms and side torsos, and a Coventry-6 SRM-6 launcher. This energy-heavy loadout grants the Guillotine excellent sustained combat endurance with minimal logistical requirements, though the design has been plagued by persistent weapon system quirks. The Sunglow laser's fiber optic power cabling runs near the surface of the underarm and can bind when the weapon is raised above shoulder level, while the SRM launcher has a stubborn tendency to fail to arm its fifth and sixth missiles. Twenty-five single heat sinks on the original model allow the entire weapons suite to fire simultaneously with minimal heat buildup, making the Guillotine a formidable brawler despite these idiosyncrasies.
text.deployment: This unique variant is believed to be a ComStar prototype that was delivered in error to the Free Rasalhague Republic's 1st Drakøns in 3049, intended as a gift from ComStar. The modification replaces ten single heat sinks with fifteen double-strength models, swaps the left arm large laser for an ER PPC, and dramatically increases the medium laser count from four to twelve units distributed across the head, right arm, left torso, and right torso. The SRM-6 rack and its ammunition bay are retained. While this loadout provides devastating close-range firepower, the excessive heat generation from a full alpha strike makes careful fire discipline essential.
text.battleHistory:
The Guillotine's combat history spans over six centuries of near-continuous service. Designed in 2499 as a front-line heavy for the Terran Hegemony, it set the standard against which later heavy BattleMechs would be measured. Known for its mobility, armor, and dependable mix of weapons, the Guillotine anchored fast attack units alongside designs like the Griffin and Thunderbolt, providing heavy fire support for entire companies. With the rise of the Star League, the design became a fixture of nearly every SLDF regiment, though heavier and more sophisticated machines eventually pushed it into the role of a heavy raider.

The fall of the Star League scattered Guillotines across all the Great Houses, while ComStar seized the largest intact stockpile after raiding the former Newhart facilities on New Earth in 2788, acquiring close to a battalion's worth of machines. Newhart's factory had already been destroyed in 2776 during the Amaris Civil War, leaving Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as the sole remaining producer. Lycomb-Davion IntroTech had also manufactured the Guillotine from their facility on Demeter, but Capellan Confederation forces destroyed this plant early in the First Succession War. As the Succession Wars ground on, shortages of advanced components forced Irian to develop the downgraded GLT-4L, which they produced intermittently for the next several centuries.

During the Second Succession War, House Marik employed Guillotines to devastating effect as guerrilla raiders against Capellan worlds, exploiting the design's energy-based weapons and jump capability to strike military support facilities and industries with impunity. Two dozen Guillotines ranged across half a dozen worlds, hiding in unpopulated areas and appearing at random, tying up Confederation forces until Marik troops captured the worlds of Ohrensen and Ilmachna. ComStar's stockpile fed machines to both their Com Guards and, covertly, to the Ghost Regiments of the Draconis Combine.

The recovery of the Helm Memory Core in the late 3040s breathed new life into the design. Irian's GLT-5M model, produced from a refurbished plant originally established under a Newhart license, not only restored the Guillotine to its Star League-era capabilities but improved upon them with more reliable weaponry. The design continued to evolve through the FedCom Civil War, which saw the introduction of the Federated Suns' GLT-8D refit, and the Jihad, when Irian Technologies produced the GLT-6WB and GLT-6WB2 variants for the Word of Blake. Production has continued into the Dark Age and ilClan eras from Irian's facilities on both Irian and Angell II, with the GLT-7M representing the latest evolution of this venerable design.

text.overview: In and out of production for over 600 years, the Guillotine is a ’Mech with a long and storied career. Even wide usage by the Word of Blake could not diminish its legend. A mild evolution of the GLT-5M, the -7M boosts the Guillotine’s long-range firepower with a capacitor-boosted ER PPC backed-up by twin light PPCs. A pair of ER medium lasers and an ammo-efficient Streak SRM 6 round out the weaponry. Durability is enhanced with CASE II, which reputedly also corrects the intermittent missile arming problems that plagued the original system from its inception.
text.notableUnits: Captain Mattheo Orloff: A distant relative of the ruling Orloff family, Mattheo Orloff earned his commission in the First Orloff Grenadiers through his own efforts rather than via nepotism. During the Operation Triumvir attacks on Sophie’s World in August 3146, the Grenadiers stalemated the First Regulan Hussars for over two months before forcing their withdrawal. Orloff and his company were instrumental in this. He constantly used his Guillotine’s mobility and endurance to harass Regulan positions.:br::tab:Following the assassination of Captain-General Jessica Marik, the Orloff Grenadiers were among the first League troops to take the war to the Regulan Fiefs. The Grenadiers landed on Tiber, backed by elements of our own Clan’s Spina Khanate, and faced off against the now-defending First Regulan Hussars. The Hussars put up a stiff fight, but they were quickly pushed back to the Earthwerks-FWL facility in Umbria City. Orloff used the mountainous terrain to close the noose on the Regulans, jumping in and out of cover and sniping away at the Hussars. For his part in forcing the Regulans’ retreat, Orloff should soon be promoted to major.
